Subject: Recap: Hydra Health discovery & sponsor alignment — next steps

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared next-step plan. I copied a short attachment (RINF-HYDRA-MAP.pdf) that maps the stakeholders and procurement path you described.

Key points from the call:
- Champion: Olivia Barnes (Clinical Ops) — will lead internal pilot & demo coordination.
- Economic buyer: Michael Gomez, SVP Finance — cares about unit economics and headcount savings.
- Security/legal: security will need SOC 2 + VPC/network diagrams; procurement will own contract cadence.
- Primary criteria: latency under 300ms for triage flows, cost per API call target ~$0.01, and offline auditability for compliance.

Action items we agreed:
1) Redwood to share tailored exec one-pager + an ROI sketch for Michael (Laura/Vivek) — ETA Tue 18 Aug.
2) Olivia to introduce Michael and procurement (procurement@hydrahealth.com) to the thread or a short intro email — ETA Mon 17 Aug.
3) Redwood to upload SOC2 evidence checklist + sample controls (Marissa) — attaching SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx.
4) Schedule 30-min technical deep dive with your security team — proposed windows next week.

Attachments: RINF-HYDRA-MAP.pdf (stakeholder map, buying path)

Open questions we flagged: whether the pilot will run on de-identified PHI or purely metadata, and whether the procurement team requires vendor security questionnaire completion prior to PO.

Next step: Olivia — if you can share a short intro to Michael + procurement, we’ll fast-track the exec one-pager and compliance pack.

Thanks — Laura

Thanks, Laura — great recap and appreciate the stakeholder map. A few clarifications from our side: 

- I’ll intro Michael Gomez and our procurement alias (procurement@hydrahealth.com) on Monday. Michael is the fiscal approver; he wants a concise ROI and an implementation timeline that aligns to Q4 budget planning.
- Security: our InfoSec lead (cc'ed below when I intro) will want the SOC2 evidence pack and network architecture. PHI: for the pilot we will use fully de-identified records but will want to confirm data handling in the contract.
- Decision criteria: execs prioritize hard-dollar ROI (FTE saved / faster throughput), risk posture, and a tight SLA around availability.

Requests for Redwood: 
1) Please send an exec one-pager highlighting projected savings and case study bullets for a healthcare triage pilot (single page) — we need this for Michael.
2) Can you provide a short talk track (3 bullets) Olivia can use when I introduce you to Michael? He prefers direct, ROI-first messaging.
3) Is there a template NDA? We can sign an NDA if you need it before sharing some of the security artifacts.

Looking forward to the intros Monday.

Best,

Hi Olivia — adding the materials you requested. Attached: Hydra-exec-onepager.pdf (one-page ROI sketch) and SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (fill-in). Also below are three tight talk-track bullets you can use for Michael: 

1) Immediate ROI: Pilot projects often show a 20–30% reduction in triage time; for a team of 10 clinicians this translates to ~0.8 FTE equivalent saved in month 1.
2) Low-risk path: Pilot on de-identified data, isolated VPC, audit logs retained for 1 year — we can include contractual language for audit support.
3) Economics & scaling: Start with a month-long pilot (X tokens/day cap); we’ll model spend and show projected per-interaction costs at steady-state.

Procurement note for your team: if Hydra requires additional security artifacts beyond SOC2 (e.g., penetration test report), let us know — we’ll surface available docs or propose a timeboxed remediation plan.

Karthik — quick ask: if Hydra pushes for a pilot discount or a committed pilot price, what is our authorized concession for a healthcare PoC? Please advise so we can set correct expectations with Michael.

Attachments: Hydra-exec-onepager.pdf, SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx

Thanks — Marissa
